thread.title: Vermont Agency of Education shares weekly updates and opportunities for students and educators

author: D. A. Aranda
title: Vermont Agency of Education shares weekly updates and opportunities for students and educators
text:
Zoie Saunders, Secretary | Vermont Agency of Education
The Vermont Agency of Education released its Weekly Field Memo on May 6, providing recent news, upcoming events, and items of interest for the education community.
The memo includes a call for applications from Vermont secondary students interested in serving as a student member on the State Board of Education. The position is a two-year term with rising sophomores and juniors encouraged to apply by submitting materials by Wednesday, May 20. Questions about the board can be directed to Maureen Gaidys at the Agency of Education.
An informational session will be held on May 20 for educators interested in using grant funds to promote college and career readiness. The session will focus on enabling teachers to become credentialed as adjunct faculty so they can offer concurrent college courses within high schools. No preregistration is required.
Additional highlights include virtual training sessions from the Vermont School Boards Association for new school board members, open voting for the 2025-2026 Vermont Youth Book Awards until June 1, and resources available through the "Confident Kids" campaign aimed at helping adults support children’s confidence around food and movement. The memo also recognizes School Nurse Appreciation Day on May 6, thanking nurses across Vermont schools for their contributions.
Professional development opportunities are being offered this month by the Vermont Department of Health for sexual health educators. These include a full-day workshop on comprehensive sexual education and a community practice session focused on managing misinformation and strengthening partnerships between teachers and administrators.
The memo addresses deployment impacts on students with family members in the Vermont National Guard, noting an upcoming webinar scheduled for May 19 that will cover strategies to support affected students. Finally, several job openings at the Agency are listed as part of ongoing recruitment efforts.
